summary: @iobandamwer/native-helper ships a sandbox-evading native loader that drops and executes an encrypted payload on install
details: On install, package.json's postinstall hook loads a shipped native addon (addon.node on Linux, addon_win.node on Windows) and invokes its init() entry point. The Linux addon contains the string set required to read a co-located encrypted blob (./.napi_cache, 6,052,359 bytes, sha256 5d46919dac8d89a164b87ef1246767e0e24141a55175514dfd597a73983a9279, zero printable strings) from the user's HOME, write a decoded executable to /tmp/.<uid>, chmod it, and fork+setsid+execlp it as a detached daemon. Before executing, the addon checks for CI providers (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NETLIFY, VERCEL, SCREWDRIVER, CF_BUILD_ID, SANDBOX), container indicators (/proc/1/cgroup, docker, containerd, kubepod, podman, dockerinit), and debugger presence (/proc/self/status TracerPid, /proc/self/maps), suppressing execution in those environments so the payload fires only on real developer or production hosts. The README's self-description as a 'temporary placeholder for staged publishing' is inconsistent with shipping an evasion-gated native loader and an encrypted 6 MB executable blob.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
